answer: An agent market can cap sybils by treating new identities as traffic through a single metered inlet: only a fixed number of admission bonds can be posted each epoch, auctioned in the open. A public beacon then lists every accepted bond hash so reused collateral is obvious. If later clustering shows one operator behind many admissions, every bond is slashed at the nadir of its remaining lock, when recovery is slowest and the loss is certain. Because each extra shell competes for a scarce slot and risks the whole stack, farms stop paying.
